transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-16
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Tom Harris (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM), Luis Martinez (BlueWave PM), Aisha Khan (BlueWave Infra), Sara Blake (BlueWave Security), Mark Chen (CTO, joined at 15:22)

-- Auto-generated summary (may be noisy):
Priya notes a regression on p95 after recent model tweak, we look at batch sizes, KV cash warming, and networking latencies. Customer worries about SSO and audit logs; action items assigned.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Tom Harris: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll try to keep to 45 minutes but we got 52 on the calendar so, uh, appreciate the time. quick roll call?
[00:08] Luis Martinez: Luis here, platform PM. Aisha's on infra, sara on security, Mark will join in a bit.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Aisha, yep.
[00:13] Sara Blake: Sara joining.
[00:15] Tom Harris: Awesome. Priya, Evan, wanna kick off with the regression findings?
[00:20] Priya Nair: Yeah sure. So, last week we pushed the updated quantized op chain for the model variant, and on staging we saw p95 jump from ~320ms to ~610ms for 1k-token sessions. p50 is fine, p95 and p99 are where the reg shows. we looked at batching config, there's a small change in continuous batching alignment and the k-v cache warmup isn't hitting as fast. also noticed a small network egress tail around 200 to 300ms for cold starts, looks like DNS resolution and NAT gateway udp latency.
[00:46] Evan Cho: To add, we also saw memory thrashing when sequence length spiked; the runtime was resizing allocations which adds jitter. may be correlated with our kernel choice for layer norm on the quantized path.
[01:04] Luis Martinez: Hmm, okay. the spike is concerning. we're simulating typical inbound traffic; our users do a lot of long-context queries. what's the tradeoff on quantization plus these kernel choices vs just running fp16 on dedicated?
[01:18] Priya Nair: good question. quantization buys token-cost savings but can interact poorly with certain fused kernels on older drivers. fp16 on dedicated hardware gives more predictable tail latency. We recommended a small dedicated pool for the POC to hit SLOs while we tune quantization for cost.
[01:33] Aisha Khan: On networking side, we did notice NAT translation limits on our side for the staging subnets - we can bump them but want to know the egress IPs from Redwood for firewall rules.
[01:44] Tom Harris: We'll send the egress IP list; Maya will drop the network diagram. Also, Redwood supports VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on your cloud - both work but PrivateLink avoids NAT egress.
[01:58] Sara Blake: quick sec, on compliance: we saw audit events but need SAML assertions captured and KMS envelopes for key wrapping. are those surfaced in the console logs?
[02:09] Evan Cho: The control plane records audit traces; we can emit SAML metadata and show KMS key IDs in the audit log. We'll need to confirm whether you want Customer-Managed KMS vs Redwood-managed. There may be slight perf delta if keys are in a remote HSM.
[02:26] Luis Martinez: We prefer CMK in our HSM, but need to measure the latency impact. any ballpark?
[02:30] Priya Nair: HSM signing adds a couple of milliseconds per request for small ops, but for token-level crypto we typically cache envelopes, so the amortized hit is low. If you do envelope decryption on every token it's expensive; we recommend envelope caching + in-memory keywrap for session duration.
[02:48] Aisha Khan: noted. we'll validate with our security team.
[02:51] Tom Harris: Back to the regression; Priya, what remediation steps did you try?
[02:55] Priya Nair: We rolled back kernel selection to the older fused kernels and re-ran the batch with forced kv-cache warmup. p95 came down to ~350ms but p99 still had awkward spikes at 750 so there's more investigating. suspecting a combination of kernel choice + network tail on cold starts.
[03:13] Luis Martinez: Could that be a DNS resolver issue? our staging uses a shared resolver with aggressive timeouts.
[03:18] Evan Cho: Possibly. We captured tcp traces and saw a handful of sub-second stalls aligned with resolver timeouts. If we pin DNS in the pod or use egress via PrivateLink (no NAT) the tail disappears in our tests.
[03:32] Aisha Khan: PrivateLink would be ideal, but we have to review cost. also want to highlight that our compliance team wants no external egress without explicit approval.
[03:41] Tom Harris: Understood. we can do VPC peering + private IP routes; that avoids egress. we'll share config snippets.
[03:47] Sara Blake: About audit logs — will you redact PII? we can't have PHI in logs going off-net.
[03:53] Evan Cho: Yes, we support log redaction rules; by default we do not retain PII. We'll share the retention and redaction configs.
[03:59] Priya Nair: Another note: for the warmup profile, the first 10 sessions cost more tokens during KV prime; if your traffic pattern has many cold sessions we should pre-warm or use a prefix cache. That's part of the bench we'll run.
[04:15] Luis Martinez: Okay makes sense. two paths sound possible: 1) small dedicated pool (fp16) for SLOs while we tune quantization and the other kernels; or 2) stay hosted but use PrivateLink/VPC peering and aggressive warming. what's your recommendation?
[04:28] Tom Harris: For pilot quick wins, dedicated small pool is fastest to hit tail SLOs. For long term, peering + quantization tuned would be best for cost. we'll put numbers in the pricing sketch.
[04:38] Aisha Khan: For the dedicated option, what's the expected commit size for a small pool?
[04:42] Tom Harris: We'll draft two options: small dedicated (reserved 4-GPU equivalent) and tiny reserved (2-GPU burst). numbers will be in the action.
[04:51] Mark Chen: (joins) Sorry for being late — what am I walking into?
[04:55] Tom Harris: Hey Mark, quick recap — we saw p95 regressions on staging tied to kernel + q8 ops and some network egress tail. We discussed peering and dedicated pool options.
[05:07] Mark Chen: Got it. Is this showing up in production traffic?
[05:10] Priya Nair: Minimal in prod so far; most of our repros are on staging workload that simulates longer contexts. But we want to be sure before ramping.
[05:18] Mark Chen: Ok — needed to know. Also what's the plan for a failover test? we need deterministic fallback when the model times out.
[05:25] Evan Cho: We can configure fallback routing rules: when p95 or error rate crosses threshold, route to a smaller faster model variant or to dedicated pool. Redwood supports automated fallbacks and we can show your app how to use the policy in the control plane.
[05:38] Luis Martinez: Can you show us a sample fallback policy?
[05:41] Priya Nair: Yes we'll share a sample policy file and a quick script to toggle canary routing.
[05:46] Aisha Khan: On credentials— we're worried about short-lived creds for pods. what's the refresh window?
[05:50] Tom Harris: Our gateway issues short-lived tokens by default; you can exchange them via STS for longer lived ones if needed. We also can support federated SAML SSO to avoid long-lived secrets.
[05:58] Sara Blake: For audits, we need a map of who accessed models and which key was used. is that in the audit logs?
[06:03] Evan Cho: Yes. The logs show authentication principal, model id, and key_id. We can expand to include session_id and request trace id for correlated tracing.
[06:12] Luis Martinez: Perfect. Alright, next, can we talk briefly about the benchmark plan?
[06:18] Priya Nair: Sure. Proposed: a 2-step bench. Step 1: 2k-session run to validate fixes (quick). Step 2: 10k-session ramp with synthetic long context patterns to measure tail and cache warmup. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, token cost, and trace-level spans. We want to run step 1 this week and step 2 next week.
[06:38] Luis Martinez: Good. what infra do you need?
[06:41] Priya Nair: Staging cluster creds, peering info or PrivateLink endpoint, and a baseline workload script. we'll provide the script; you provide network & auth. Also a list of sample keys for KMS integration testing or a staging key to run envelope tests.
[06:56] Aisha Khan: We'll share peering config, but can't open outbound network until we confirm egress IPs.
[07:02] Tom Harris: We'll send the list immediately after the call.
[07:05] Evan Cho: For the traces, please enable high sampling on the staging control plane for the run so we can get full spans. Without high sampling some p99 events are missed.
[07:16] Sara Blake: Regarding PII redaction, can you redact at the agent level before logs leave our VPC?
[07:21] Evan Cho: We have an SDK filter to remove PII client-side; we recommend enabling it. We'll share implementation notes.
[07:29] Priya Nair: Also, a note about our checkpoint and KV cache: If your workload generates a lot of unique prefixes, pre-warming might not help. We need the workload distribution. Luis, can you share a sample of request length distribution?
[07:43] Luis Martinez: Yep, I'll export and share.
[07:46] Tom Harris: On the timing — we aim for step 1 run by Friday, step 2 next Wednesday. Sound okay?
[07:53] Aisha Khan: Friday's tight but possible for step 1.
[07:57] Mark Chen: Make sure to include an ops runbook for toggling fallbacks. we don't want surprises during business hours.
[08:04] Tom Harris: We'll include an ops runbook.
[08:06] Luis Martinez: Any other blockers?
[08:09] Priya Nair: We still need the SAML metadata to set up federated auth in staging.
[08:13] Sara Blake: I'll send SAML metadata today.
[08:16] Aisha Khan: And we'll share the VPC peering template and the firewall rules doc.
[08:20] Evan Cho: One more point — we tracked a rare oom in a node during long context runs, looks like an allocator misreporting. we'll pin a newer runtime build in our next test which fixes the tracking bug. That should remove some jitter.
[08:34] Luis Martinez: Good. please call out if the build change causes any functional diffs.
[08:38] Priya Nair: Will do, we'll validate on a small canary.
[08:41] Tom Harris: Okay, let's recap and close.
[08:43] Tom Harris: Recap: Redwood will run the staged regression tests (Priya) and share traces; will send egress IPs and network diagram (Maya); will provide a pricing sketch for a small dedicated pool (Tom); customer to share SAML metadata and VPC peering info (Sara, Aisha); schedule security Q/A (Maya + Sara).
[09:05] Luis Martinez: Thanks all. If we get the bench results and the pricing by Monday we'll decide whether to spin up the small dedicated pool for the pilot.
[09:12] Tom Harris: Great. we'll get those items over. thanks everyone.
[09:15] (meeting ends)

-- End of transcript. Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings: "KV cache" appears as "K-V cash" in a couple places, and "PrivateLink" sometimes transcribed as "private link"; speaker overlaps at join times.
file_notes: POC weekly sync focusing on environment readiness, access, and a regression bench. Avoid creating PHI in logs for POCs; use redaction SDK. Customer leaning to dedicated for pilot but wants quantization tuned for cost.
